When data['shelf_life'] is non-empty and inventory is modeled as I[p,l,t,r], introduce explicit per-bucket sell variables s_r[p,l,t,r] with s_r[p,l,t,r] <= I[p,l,t,r], FIFO exhaustion (s_r[p,l,t,r] = 0 for all r > 1 whenever I[p,l,t,1] > 0), and a linking equality sales[p,l,t] = sum_r s_r[p,l,t,r] that feeds the C-DEMAND balance. Without this coupling the scalar sales variable in C-DEMAND is decoupled from the age-bucketed stock, so the optimizer cannot draw on existing inventory and the demand equality becomes infeasible. Do NOT write C-DEMAND with a bare sales[p,l,t] free variable when the r-dimension is active.
trigger: data['shelf_life'] is a non-empty mapping (at least one product p has shelf_life[p] >= 1), which activates the 4-D inventory variable I[p,l,t,r]

origin.rationale: All 58 failing cells share shelf-life (remaining-life) tracking; the demand-balance constraint references a single sales[p,l,t] that is never constrained to the sum of I[p,l,t,r] buckets, so the solver cannot convert on-hand inventory into sales and the equality is infeasible (balance driven negative or to zero while demand > 0).
origin.win_safety: When data['shelf_life'] is absent or empty the inventory variable is the standard 3-D I[p,l,t]; the sum over r collapses to the single bucket, s_r reduces to the existing sales <= I[p,l,t] bound already present in the base model, and no new variable or constraint is introduced—behavior on all previously-passing cells is bit-identical.

text: Model each (product, location) pair as an independent inventory node with balance I[p,l,t+1] = I[p,l,t] + x[p,l,t] - s[p,l,t] - w[p,l,t]; constrain s[p,l,t] <= D[p,l,t] so unmet demand is lost (not backordered) and penalized; constrain sum_l x[p,l,t] <= Cap[p,t] for per-product production; enforce I[p,l,t] >= 0 for all t. Do NOT introduce any inter-location flow or transfer variables.
trigger: data contains demand[product][location][period], production_capacity[product][period], initial_inventory[product][location], and NO transshipment/transfer edge list (single-echelon, no inter-location movement)

origin.rationale: All three verified cells (52-week, base, high-waste) share this exact local-balance structure: independent per-(product,location) inventory states, capacity-constrained replenishment, lost-sales (not backorder) demand fulfillment, and zero coupling between locations. The auditor confirmed conservation and initial-condition correctness only when each node was self-contained.
origin.win_safety: The trigger requires the ABSENCE of a transshipment/transfer edge list. Any cell that does contain inter-location movement fields will not match this trigger, so multi-echelon or transshipment cells are unaffected and will be handled by their own clauses.

text: When the scenario's structure cues do NOT contain a "shelf life" field and inventory is indexed only as I[p,l,t], apply the standard single-cohort balance I[p,l,t] = I[p,l,t-1] + prod[p,l,t] - sales[p,l,t] - waste[p,l,t] with the demand constraint sales[p,l,t] + lost[p,l,t] = demand[p,l,t]. EXCLUSION: if the structure cues contain "Shelf life" and the variable definition introduces a remaining-life index r (I[p,l,t,r], r=1 oldest/FIFO), the single-cohort scalar formulation must NOT be used; sales in period t must be allocated across age-cohorts starting from r=1, and the C-DEMAND balance must equal the sum of sales actually drawn from all cohorts consumed in that period. Applying a naive scalar sales variable when cohort tracking is active decouples sales+lost from true demand, producing negative or zero C-DEMAND residuals.
trigger: scenario structure_cues contain the string "shelf life" AND variable_definition introduces a remaining-life index r (I[p,l,t,r])

origin.rationale: All three verified successes (base, 52-weeks, high_waste_v0) use a single-index inventory with no remaining-life dimension, so the scalar demand balance closes exactly. All three failures (high_waste_v3, jit_logic_v3, cannibalization_v1) introduce I[p,l,t,r] with FIFO shelf-life cohorts; the solver then emits a single sales[p,l,t] that does not reconcile with the per-cohort outflows, leaving the C-DEMAND residual non-zero.
origin.win_safety: The trigger requires both the literal string "shelf life" in structure_cues AND the r-indexed variable in the definition. Cells like retail_f1_base_v0, retail_f1_52_weeks_v0, and retail_f1_high_waste_v0 contain neither, so the clause's exclusion branch is never entered and the standard single-cohort formulation is applied unchanged.

text: Model each (product, location) pair as an independent inventory node with balance I[p,l,t+1] = I[p,l,t] + x[p,l,t] - s[p,l,t] - w[p,l,t] for t >= 1; FIX initial inventory I[p,l,1] = I0[p,l] (declared starting stock, typically 0) as a hard equality, not a free variable; constrain s[p,l,t] <= D[p,l,t] so unmet demand is lost (not backordered) and penalized via w[p,l,t] = D[p,l,t] - s[p,l,t]; constrain sum_l x[p,l,t] <= Cap[p,t]; enforce I[p,l,t] >= 0. Do NOT introduce inter-location flow variables. EXCLUSION: do NOT apply when the cell has no substitution/transfer edges (no_substitution family) — leave its native balance, initial-stock, and demand constraints untouched.
trigger: substitution_edges non-empty AND NOT no_substitution family
